problem: The description mixes two different protocols. It first says the receiver maintains a receive window of size N to buffer out‑of‑order frames (Selective‑Repeat behavior) and later says that if a frame is lost the receiver discards it and all later frames (Go‑Back‑N behavior). This contradiction can confuse students.
fix: Choose one protocol and describe it consistently. For example, for the basic Go‑Back‑N sliding‑window: remove the sentence about buffering out‑of‑order frames and keep the discard rule. Or, for Selective‑Repeat: keep the buffering sentence and replace the discard rule with “the receiver stores out‑of‑order frames and sends duplicate ACKs for the missing sequence number.”

where: Section 2: Sliding‑window flow control, bullet "When ACK = k arrives, sender slides window to start at k and may send new frame k+N‑1."
problem: The wording is ambiguous about which new frame can be sent after the window slides.
fix: Clarify: "When ACK = k arrives, the sender slides its window so that the lowest unacknowledged sequence number becomes k. It can then transmit any new frames with sequence numbers from k+N up to the new window limit (i.e., up to k+N‑1 if they have not been sent yet)."
